title: Customer Tool Card: Declaring the Value a Piece Is Handed Over At
content:
A piece handed to Belrose under the Belrose Trade-In and Upgrade Programmes is put on the record at a value while it is in the chain's care, together with the appraisal that value rests on.

## Whose action this is

The declaration is the customer's own, because it is their property that is being held. The tool `confirm_custody_declaration_bb764f94` is unlocked and handed over, and the customer themselves runs it. It takes their confirmed declaration onto the upgrade desk's request record for that trade-in registration, carrying the value they are putting the piece in at while it is in the chain's care, and writes onto the registration itself the appraisal the declaration rests on. The request stands as confirmed by the customer from the moment of the call, and the desk can see both the figure declared and the appraisal behind it.

## Parameters

- `credit_reference` — the reference number of the trade-in registration the piece was taken in on, written on the customer's upgrade paperwork as TU- followed by six digits; the desk reads it from the registration lookup.
- `declared_custody_value` — the value the customer is putting the piece in at, in USD to 2 decimal places, a plain positive number with no currency symbol and no thousands separator; the tool stores it rounded to 2 decimal places by half-up arithmetic at the moment of the call.
- `appraisal_reference` — the appraisal the declaration rests on, written as AP- followed by six digits, for example AP-660412, in upper case with the hyphen kept and no spaces; it is taken from the appraisal engagement carried out on the piece.

## What comes back

A one-line confirmation naming the registration reference, the reference number of the request record just taken, the value declared in USD to 2 decimal places and the appraisal it rests on. A string beginning "Error" means nothing was written; any other string means the declaration stands confirmed on the record.
